chunks: And the confirmation of that is what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Muhtadī, from Saʿīd ibn Saʿd, who said:

I asked him—meaning Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام—about a man who had a son whom he claimed, then he disowned him and excluded him from the inheritance, while I am his executor, so what should I do?
So he عليه السلام said: “The child remains binding upon him because of his acknowledgment in public view. The executor must not withhold him from anything that he already knows [to be established].”

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: inheritance due from the deceased's estate
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child or son whose lineage is under discussion
key_terms.بِالْمَشْهَدِ: in public view or in a witnessed setting
key_terms.عَلِمَهُ: knew it, i.e. knew it to be established
key_terms.لِإِقْرَارِهِ: because of his prior acknowledgment or admission
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: his executor, the one entrusted to carry out his estate instructions
key_terms.يَدْفَعْهُ: to repel, deny, or withhold him

ai.seo_question: If a father publicly acknowledged a son and later disowned him, can the executor exclude him from the inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning lineage and inheritance when a father had previously acknowledged a son publicly and later attempted to deny him. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام rules that the prior acknowledgment stands, and the executor may not deprive the son of rights that are already established and known.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5516 - And the confirmation of this is what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdul Aziz ibn Al-Muhtadi from Sa'id ibn Sa'd, who said:

'I asked Imam (as) - meaning Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) - about a man who had a son whom he acknowledged and then later disowned, excluding him from the inheritance. I am his executor, so what should I do?'
Imam (as) said: "The son remains legally his due to his prior public acknowledgment. The executor cannot deny him anything that is already known."
